### Executive Summary
- **SaaS supply-chain risk spike:** ConnectWise cloud backup compromise reportedly enabled access across **173 Microsoft 365 tenants** via stolen app credentials/permissions—assume similar OAuth app abuse patterns could hit financial orgs.
- **Multiple “exploitation-ready” edge/app RCEs:** New/reshared PoCs and toolkits for **RouterOS (MikroTik) auth bypass chain**, **Fortinet RCE**, and **WSUS SoapFormatter RCE** increase likelihood of opportunistic scanning and rapid weaponization.
- **Web app ecosystem targeting continues:** Mass-exploit tooling for **WordPress plugin RCE/file upload** and **React/Next.js RCE claims** means heightened risk for any internet-facing marketing/microsite estates and CI/CD exposure.

---

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

**1) Microsoft 365 tenant compromise via ConnectWise cloud backup (supply-chain / OAuth app abuse)**
- **What happened:** ConnectWise suspended its cloud backup service after attackers used a stolen app credential with broad Microsoft 365 permissions to compromise many tenants (reported: **173**).
- **Why it matters operationally:** This is a **direct path to mailbox/SharePoint/OneDrive access** via OAuth—bypasses MFA if attacker holds valid app creds/consents (common precursor to fraud, BEC, data theft).
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** **Review Entra ID audit logs for new/modified service principals + admin consent events**; **hunt for anomalous Graph/API activity by backup/third-party apps** and disable/suspend suspicious enterprise apps.

**2) MikroTik RouterOS “MikroTrick” chain / SSH public-key auth bypass PoC (CVE-2026-67276)**
- **What happened:** A lab PoC was published for **CVE-2026-67276** (RouterOS SSH public-key auth bypass) tied to an actively exploited “MikroTrick” chain per CERT PL context.
- **Why it matters operationally:** Internet-edge routers are high-impact footholds; compromise enables **traffic manipulation, lateral movement, and credential theft**—especially relevant for branch/ATM/partner connectivity.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** **Verify RouterOS inventory + exposed management (SSH/Winbox/API) and isolate from internet**; **prioritize emergency patch/upgrade and rotate keys/passwords** where exposure is confirmed.

**3) Fortinet product unauthenticated RCE PoC (CVE-2025-32756)**
- **What happened:** A PoC was released for **CVE-2025-32756** (AuthHash cookie processing) impacting multiple Fortinet products (per summary: FortiVoice/FortiMail/FortiNDR/etc.).
- **Why it matters operationally:** Fortinet devices are frequently targeted for initial access; PoC publication increases **mass scanning and edge exploitation** likelihood within days.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** **Check perimeter exposure and current firmware versions; fast-track patching/mitigations**; **monitor for suspicious requests/cookies to Fortinet web interfaces** and unusual process/network activity from the appliance management plane.

**4) WSUS SoapFormatter RCE PoC (CVE-2025-59287 / CVE-2023-35317)**
- **What happened:** Public PoC tooling was posted for **WSUS-related SoapFormatter RCE** (CVE-2025-59287), referencing prior research and a related CVE.
- **Why it matters operationally:** WSUS is privileged infrastructure; compromise can enable **software distribution abuse** and rapid domain-wide ransomware staging.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** **Confirm WSUS servers and enforce network restrictions (limit who can talk to WSUS/admin endpoints)**; **hunt for unusual WSUS service behavior, spawned processes, or new scheduled tasks** on WSUS hosts.

**5) Web app mass exploitation toolkits (WordPress plugins + React/Next.js RCE claims)**
- **What happened:** Mass-exploit code surfaced for **WordPress Divi Form Builder unauth RCE (CVE-2026-5524)** and **WP Activity Log PHP object injection (CVE-2026-54806)**; separate “React2Shell” repo claims **React Server Components/Next.js RCE (CVE-2025-55182 / CVE-2025-66478)**.
- **Why it matters operationally:** Even if core banking isn’t WordPress/React, **marketing domains, customer comms portals, and third-party microsites** often are—and they’re commonly used for phishing, watering holes, and credential theft.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** **Scan external web estate for affected plugins/framework versions and remove/patch fast**; **monitor WAF/web logs for file upload attempts, webshell indicators, and sudden admin account creation** (assume exploit kits will automate this).

---

### Monitoring & detection recommendations
- **Entra ID / M365 (ConnectWise theme):** Monitor **Enterprise App consent**, **service principal credential additions**, and **Graph API spikes** in Entra audit/sign-in logs (ATT&CK **T1528** Steal App Access Token, **T1098** Account Manipulation).
- **CASB/Cloud App Security:** Alert on **mass mailbox item access, unusual eDiscovery/Content Search**, abnormal OneDrive/SharePoint downloads by app identities (ATT&CK **T1213** Data from Information Repositories).
- **Edge network devices (MikroTik/Fortinet):** From firewall/VPN/IDS logs, hunt for **internet scanning bursts** to management ports and repeated auth anomalies; correlate with **new outbound connections from network appliances** to unfamiliar IPs (ATT&CK **T1190** Exploit Public-Facing Application).
- **WSUS server telemetry:** On WSUS hosts, flag **w3wp/wsusservice spawning cmd/powershell**, new services, scheduled tasks, or unusual child processes (ATT&CK **T1059** Command and Scripting Interpreter, **T1543** Create/Modify System Process).
- **Web/WAF logs (WordPress/plugin exploitation):** Detect **suspicious multipart uploads**, writes to uncommon extensions, requests to **/wp-content/uploads/** followed by execution attempts; monitor for **new wp-admin user creation** and login from new geos.
- **CI/CD & repo security (GhostAction/GitHub Actions theme):** Review GitHub audit logs for **workflow file changes**, newly added **secrets access**, and unexpected **OIDC/token usage** (ATT&CK **T1552** Unsecured Credentials, **T1649** Steal or Forge Auth Certificates/Keys—use as conceptual mapping).
- **Linux kernel privesc chatter (local escalation CVEs):** On Linux fleets, alert on **sudden privilege escalations**, kernel exploit patterns, and anomalous Bluetooth/vsock activity where relevant (ATT&CK **T1068** Exploitation for Privilege Escalation).

---

### Medium-term follow-ups
- **Third-party SaaS governance:** Tighten policy for **OAuth enterprise apps** (least privilege, admin consent workflow, periodic app credential rotation, and automatic disable on risky permissions).
- **Router/edge hardening program:** Ensure **management plane is never internet-exposed**, enforce jump-host access, and implement configuration drift monitoring for RouterOS/Fortinet estates.
- **Patch backlog triage:** Validate exposure and patch status for **WSUS**, Fortinet products, and any **Ivanti EPM** footprint (CVE-2024-29824 PoC resurfaced) using asset inventory + vulnerability management.
- **Web estate hygiene:** Inventory all external WordPress instances/plugins; implement **WAF rules for upload abuse** and require **MFA/admin IP allowlists** for CMS consoles.
- **Apache Camel OAuth component:** If used internally, plan upgrades addressing **CVE-2026-80312** (fail-open auth) and add negative-testing in staging to ensure auth failures block requests.
- **Incident prep:** Rehearse playbooks for **OAuth app compromise** (containment = disable app/SP, revoke refresh tokens, review mailbox rules, eDiscovery for data access) and for **edge device compromise** (config backup, re-image, credential rotation).

highlights.title: ConnectWise backup app breaches 173 Microsoft tenants, Chinese spies exploit BeyondTrust zero-day, Japan declares first cyber state of emergency
